findings.title: Search order controls discovery

findings.mechanism: The focus carriers for beginning, precedence, vessels, extraction, and brotherhood meet the prior finding in 12:75 and its stated consequence. The ordered relation delays the terminal vessel and makes the final extraction read as the completion of a search-shaped operation.
findings.reader_payoff: The reader can see why the order of opening matters: the result appears within a procedure that has been visibly carried through the other vessels, while the plain extraction remains intact.
findings.containment: This retains the surface sequence and does not assert that the narrated order proves impartiality or excludes a simple narrative explanation. The finding branch from 12:75 is retained as supplied source-image evidence.

epistemic.reason: Trusted channel evidence is anchored in the focus surface and the supplied 12:75 context; two nominated source-image branches remain explicitly qualified.
